subject: radiology
title: Piezoelectric Effect, Acoustic Impedance and Ultrasound Artefacts

steps.title: Piezoelectric crystals make the beam
steps.tx: **Piezoelectric effect** lets lead zirconate titanate crystals change shape when voltage is applied and generate voltage when returning echoes squeeze them. One crystal therefore transmits a pulse and then listens for its echo. Modern probes hold hundreds of elements fired in sequence to steer and focus the beam electronically. The crystal thickness sets the natural frequency, with thinner elements producing higher frequencies.
steps.say: Piezoelectric effect lets lead zirconate titanate crystals change shape when voltage is applied and generate voltage when returning echoes squeeze them. One crystal therefore transmits a pulse then listens for its echo. Modern probes hold hundreds of elements fired in sequence to steer the beam. Crystal thickness sets the natural frequency, thinner elements giving higher frequencies.

steps.title: Frequency trades depth for detail
steps.tx: **Transducer frequency** balances resolution against penetration. A 12 megahertz linear probe resolves thyroid nodules and tendons within 4 cm of the skin but cannot reach the liver. A 3.5 megahertz curvilinear probe crosses 20 cm of abdomen with coarser detail. Axial resolution improves as frequency rises because wavelength shortens, reaching fractions of a millimetre at the highest diagnostic frequencies.
steps.say: Transducer frequency balances resolution against penetration. A twelve megahertz linear probe resolves thyroid nodules and tendons within four centimetres of skin but cannot reach the liver. A three point five megahertz curved probe crosses twenty centimetres of abdomen with coarser detail. Axial resolution improves as frequency rises because wavelength shortens.

steps.title: Acoustic impedance and reflection
steps.tx: **Acoustic impedance** equals tissue density multiplied by the speed of sound in that tissue. At a boundary the fraction of beam reflected rises with the impedance gap between the two sides. Soft tissue against bone reflects strongly and casts shadow, while fluid against soft tissue reflects weakly and lets most energy through. Coupling gel removes the skin air gap that would otherwise reflect nearly the whole beam.
steps.say: Acoustic impedance equals tissue density multiplied by the speed of sound in that tissue. At a boundary the reflected fraction rises with the impedance gap between the two sides. Soft tissue against bone reflects strongly and casts shadow, while fluid reflects weakly and lets most energy through. Gel removes the skin air gap that would reflect nearly everything.

steps.title: Acoustic shadowing
steps.tx: **Acoustic shadowing** is the dark band behind a strongly reflecting or absorbing structure. Gallstones, kidney stones, ribs and bowel gas all produce it, and a clean sharp shadow behind a bright gallbladder focus is a core sign of a stone rather than a polyp. Polyps attach to the wall, do not move with posture and cast no shadow, which separates the two at the bedside.
steps.say: Acoustic shadowing is the dark band behind a strongly reflecting or absorbing structure. Gallstones, kidney stones, ribs and bowel gas all produce it, and a clean sharp shadow behind a bright gallbladder focus is a core sign of stone rather than polyp. Polyps attach to the wall, do not move with posture and cast no shadow.

steps.tx: When a structure reflects or absorbs the beam, a dark path is left behind it. That path is **acoustic shadowing**, and gallstones, renal stones, ribs and bowel gas all cast one. A bright gallbladder focus with a clean sharp shadow is read as a stone. A polyp fails the same tests: it is fixed to the wall, it does not roll when the patient changes position, and it casts no shadow. Those differences are settled at the bedside, without sending the patient for another test first.
steps.say: A clean dark trail behind a bright gallbladder focus is acoustic shadowing from a stone. Ribs, renal stones and gas cast shadows too. A polyp is attached to the wall, stays still when the patient moves, and casts no shadow, which separates it from a stone during the scan.

vis.alt: A gallbladder ultrasound shows a bright stone with a clean dark band of acoustic shadow behind it.
vis.caption: An echogenic focus inside the gallbladder throws a sharp black shadow, the ultrasound appearance of a gallstone rather than a polyp. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Posterior acoustic enhancement
steps.tx: **Posterior enhancement** is the bright band behind fluid because fluid attenuates the beam far less than solid tissue at the same depth. The scanner assumes average attenuation, so echoes returning through a cyst arrive stronger than expected and are painted brighter. Simple cysts of liver, kidney and breast all show this through transmission, which supports calling the lesion fluid rather than a solid mass.
steps.say: Posterior enhancement is the bright band behind fluid because fluid weakens the beam far less than solid tissue at the same depth. The scanner assumes average weakening, so echoes returning through a cyst arrive stronger than expected and are painted brighter. Simple cysts of liver, kidney and breast all show this through transmission, supporting a fluid diagnosis.

steps.tx: Fluid attenuates ultrasound much less than solid tissue at the same depth. The scanner still expects average loss, so echoes that have passed through a cyst return stronger than the machine predicted and are displayed too bright. The bright band is **posterior enhancement**, also called through transmission. Simple cysts of liver, kidney and breast all produce it. A solid mass would weaken the beam and darken what lies behind, so the bright trail supports fluid.
steps.say: Because fluid weakens the beam less than solid tissue, echoes behind a cyst come back stronger than the scanner expects and are painted bright. That posterior enhancement is through transmission. Liver, kidney and breast cysts all show it, which argues the lesion is fluid rather than a solid mass.

vis.alt: A renal ultrasound shows an anechoic simple cyst with a bright band of posterior acoustic enhancement behind it.
vis.caption: A simple kidney cyst is black, and the tissue immediately behind it is brighter than tissue at the same depth beside the cyst. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Reverberation and comet tail
steps.tx: **Reverberation artefact** repeats bright lines at equal intervals when sound bounces between two strong reflectors, such as the pleura and probe face. The comet tail variant tapers behind a tiny reflector like a cholesterol crystal in gallbladder adenomyomatosis or a colloid fleck in a thyroid nodule. Ring down artefact instead streams behind gas bubbles that resonate continuously, a pattern linked to bowel gas and pneumobilia.
steps.say: Reverberation artefact repeats bright lines at equal intervals when sound bounces between two strong reflectors such as pleura and probe face. The comet tail variant tapers behind a tiny reflector like a cholesterol crystal in gallbladder wall or colloid in a thyroid nodule. Ring down instead streams behind resonating gas bubbles in bowel or bile ducts.

steps.title: Mirror image artefact
steps.tx: **Mirror image artefact** duplicates a structure across a strong smooth reflector, most often the diaphragm. A liver lesion can appear again inside the lung base above the diaphragm, and colour Doppler can paint a false vessel in the mirrored copy. Moving the probe to another angle breaks the geometry and the ghost copy vanishes, confirming artefact before a lung mass is reported.

steps.title: Speed of sound assumption
steps.tx: **Sound speed** in soft tissue is taken as 1540 metres per second, and the scanner converts echo return time into depth using that single value. Fat conducts sound slower near 1450 metres per second, so structures behind thick fat are placed slightly too deep. The same assumption explains why a silicone breast implant, with much slower sound speed, distorts the apparent position of tissue behind it.
steps.say: Sound speed in soft tissue is taken as fifteen forty metres per second, and the scanner converts echo return time into depth using that single value. Fat conducts sound slower, near fourteen fifty, so structures behind thick fat are placed slightly too deep. A silicone implant distorts apparent depth the same way because its sound speed is far slower.
